Subject: Quick Q — where are LLM requests executed and how long are they retained?

Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move to procurement, our security team needs a concise answer to two items: where exactly user requests are executed (regions and subprocessors involved) and what the deletion/retention guarantees look like for transient request data and KV cache. A few specific asks: 
- Can you confirm whether any request computation or caching can cross EU borders when we pick EU-only residency?
- Which subprocessors (cloud/edge partners) could see request data in any form?
- Typical deletion SLA for ephemeral request material and full account data erasure timelines.

If you can provide a short written Q&A and any diagrams/evidence, that would help unblock legal.

Best,
Susan
Security Lead, Orion Health

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa and Jonas from Product/Infrastructure for the technical breakdown and the subprocessor inventory.

High level answers up front: 
- If you choose EU-only residency we execute requests in the selected EU regions by default and we will not intentionally route compute outside the EU.
- We have a small set of subprocessors for networking, observability, and specialized edge partners — we'll list them and evidence in the attached inventory.
- Ephemeral request data (token buffers, transient KV cache) is never written to long-term storage and is purged from runtime memory after request completion; account-level logs and persisted artifacts follow our retention policy — typical erasure SLA is 30 days for request-level artifacts and 90 days for account data deletion requests unless a longer contractual term is requested.

Marissa/Jonas — can you expand with region-by-region examples, any caveats (e.g., burst-to-us for capacity if customer opts in), and attach the flow diagram and subprocessor CSV?

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference

Susan — attaching two artifacts: 1) redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf (visual of request lifecycle) and 2) subprocessor-inventory-202808.csv (names, role, region). Key points below: 

1) Execution loci and routing rules (EU residency example)
- Primary execution nodes: Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and Amsterdam (eu-west-1) for EU residency customers.
- Smart routing: requests are routed to the nearest healthy EU cluster by latency and capacity.
- No cross-border egress: we do not route compute to non-EU regions for EU-residency unless explicit opt-in for cross-region burst is agreed.

2) Caching and KV behavior
- Runtime KV cache is in-memory on the serving node; it is not persisted to disk by default.
- Prefix and response caching for cost/latency can be configured to persist to a customer-specific blob in the chosen region (this is opt-in).

3) Subprocessors (summary)
- Cloud provider: European regions of MajorCloudCo — compute and object storage.
- Networking: FastTransit Ltd. — packet routing within EU.
- Observability: TraceSight EU (logs and traces retained under contract, separate retention).
- Optional edge partner: EdgeServe (EU POPs) — used only if customer enables low-latency edge; we can disable.

4) Deletion and retention timelines
- Transient in-memory artifacts: purged immediately after request completion (within seconds).
- Short-term diagnostic traces/logs: retained up to 7 days by default for debugging, can be reduced on request.
- Request-level persisted artifacts (if you enable debug capture or persistent caching): purged on a rolling 30-day cycle unless you request expedited erasure.
- Account deletion: we purge customer datasets and backups within 90 calendar days; we provide a certificate of deletion once completed.

5) Exceptional cases and exports
- Export controls / lawful requests: if compelled by law enforcement and the legal requirement applies in a different jurisdiction, we follow our legal escalation process and notify customers when permitted.

I've kept the inventory CSV minimal for now — it lists provider names, service role, and region. Let me know if you need contact-level DPA addenda or SOC2 report excerpts.

Regards,
Marissa
Product Security, Redwood Inference

Hi Susan — quick clarifications and next steps from infra side: 

1) FastTransit TLS behavior
- FastTransit operates as an L3/L4 transit provider within the EU; it does not terminate TLS in our standard configuration. All customer payloads are TLS-encrypted end-to-end to our EU gateways. We can provide network diagrams and a contractual statement to that effect.

2) EdgeServe and account-level toggles
- EdgeServe is opt-in per account. If disabled, no traffic is mirrored to their POPs. When enabled, data remains within EU POPs only (we maintain controls to prevent non-EU mirroring).

3) SLA language proposal (you can paste into your DPA)
- "Redwood Inference guarantees that request-level persisted artifacts will be purged within 30 calendar days following retention expiry or upon customer request for expedited deletion. Account deletion, including primary and backup artifacts, will be completed within 90 calendar days and Redwood will provide a written certificate of deletion."

4) SOC2 & cloud provider contact
- We can share a redacted SOC2 Type II report under NDA and provide MajorCloudCo EU compliance contact information to your procurement team for validation.

Next steps we suggest: 1) sign a mutual NDA so we can share the SOC2 and any contractual redactions, 2) I can schedule a 30-minute call between your security team and our infra lead to walk the flow diagram, 3) if you want, we can add the SLA clause into a redline of the DPA.

Would Tuesday at 10:00 CET work for a call?

Regards,
Jonas Weber
